requirements.original: 1) the number of the actual parameters shall be the same as the number of the formal parameters; and
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function is invoked, the number of actual parameters SHALL be the same as the number of formal parameters.
requirements.condition: a predefined function is invoked
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.2 -- 1) the number of the actual parameters shall be the same as the number of the formal parameters; and

requirements.original: 2) each actual parameter shall evaluate to an element of its corresponding formal parameter's type; and
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function is invoked, each actual parameter SHALL evaluate to an element of the type of its corresponding formal parameter.
requirements.condition: a predefined function is invoked
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.2 -- 2) each actual parameter shall evaluate to an element of its corresponding formal parameter's type; and

requirements.original: 3) all actual in and inout parameters shall be initialized with the following exceptions:
requirements.canonical: When a predefined function is invoked, every actual in and inout parameter SHALL be completely initialized, except as permitted for `lengthof`, `substr`, `replace`, `any2unistr`, `decvalue` and `decvalue_unichar`.
requirements.condition: a predefined function is invoked

improper_terms.proper: actual parameters passed to in and inout formal parameters

ambiguity.issue: 'initialized' is contrasted with 'partially initialized' in the exceptions, so 'completely initialized' (glossary) is meant; 'actual in and inout parameters' means actual parameters for in/inout formal parameters.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.2 -- 3) all actual in and inout parameters shall be initialized with the following exceptions:

requirements.original: any parameters of the functions lengthof, substr and replace may be partially initialized;
requirements.canonical: Any actual parameter of the predefined functions `lengthof`, `substr` and `replace` MAY be partially initialized.
requirements.condition: a predefined function is invoked
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.2 -- any parameters of the functions lengthof, substr and replace may be partially initialized;

requirements.original: the invalue parameter of the any2unistr function may be uninitialized or partially initialized;
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter for the `invalue` formal parameter of the `any2unistr` predefined function MAY be uninitialized or partially initialized.
requirements.condition: a predefined function is invoked
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.2 -- the invalue parameter of the any2unistr function may be uninitialized or partially initialized;

requirements.original: the encoded_value parameter of the decvalue and decvalue_unichar function may be uninitialized.
requirements.canonical: The actual parameter for the `encoded_value` formal parameter of the `decvalue` and `decvalue_unichar` predefined functions MAY be uninitialized.
requirements.condition: a predefined function is invoked

readings: Only `decvalue` and `decvalue_unichar` accept an uninitialized `encoded_value` actual parameter; for `decvalue_o` it SHALL be initialized.
`decvalue_o` (the octetstring variant, named `decvalue` in table 15) also accepts an uninitialized `encoded_value` actual parameter.
ambiguity.issue: `decvalue_o` is not listed although it has the same parameter structure; the literal reading (first) is used in canonical.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.2 -- the encoded_value parameter of the decvalue and decvalue_unichar function may be uninitialized.

requirements.original: A function may be defined within a module or be declared as being defined externally (i.e. external).
requirements.canonical: A function MAY be defined within a module or be declared as an external function (`external`).

requirements.canonical: An external function declaration SHALL NOT carry both the `@deterministic` and the `@control` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.3 -- external function [ @deterministic | @control ] ExtFunctionIdentifier "(" [ { ( FormalValuePar | FormalTemplatePar ) [","] } ] ")" [ return [ TemplateModifier ] Type ]

requirements.original: For an external function only the function interface has to be provided in the TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: An external function declaration in a TTCN-3 module SHALL provide only the function interface (no statement block).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.3 -- For an external function only the function interface has to be provided in the TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: Using the @deterministic modifier, an external function can be declared to be deterministic.
requirements.canonical: An external function MAY be declared deterministic by using the `@deterministic` modifier.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.3 -- Using the @deterministic modifier, an external function can be declared to be deterministic.

requirements.original: Deterministic functions are safe to be used when called from specific places where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects (see clause 16.1.4).
requirements.canonical: A deterministic external function IS safe to be called from the specific places listed in clause 16.1.4, where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects.

ambiguity.issue: The sentence speaks of 'deterministic functions' in general but appears in the external function clause; the glossary term 'deterministic function' is broader. Read as deterministic external functions.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.3 -- Deterministic functions are safe to be used when called from specific places where non-determinism could lead to unexpected side effects (see clause 16.1.4).

requirements.original: The @control modifier is used in the same way as described in clause 16.1.5.
requirements.canonical: The `@control` modifier of an external function IS used in the same way as for functions, as described in clause 16.1.5.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.3 -- The @control modifier is used in the same way as described in clause 16.1.5.

requirements.original: If value returning functions are called in receiving communication operations (in templates, template fields, in-line templates as actual parameters or when evaluating the port expression), in timeout operations (when evaluating the timer expression), in test component operations (in guards or events of alt statements or altsteps, see clause 20.2), or in initializations of altstep local definitions (see clause 16.2.1), the following operations shall not be present in functions called in the cases specified above, in order to avoid side effects that cause changing the state of the component or the actual snapshot and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot:
requirements.canonical: If a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation (in templates, template fields, in-line templates as actual parameters or when evaluating the port expression), in a timeout operation (when evaluating the timer expression), in a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or in the initialization of an altstep local definition, the function SHALL NOT contain any of the operations listed in clause 16.1.4 items a) to m).
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition

improper_terms.used: test component operations (in guards or events of alt statements or altsteps)
improper_terms.proper: alternatives (guards and events) of alt statements or altsteps

ambiguity.issue: 'test component operations' normally denotes create/start/stop/done etc.; the parenthesis shows that guards and events of alt statements and altsteps are meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- If value returning functions are called in receiving communication operations (in templates, template fields, in-line templates as actual parameters or when evaluating the port expression), in timeout operations (when evaluating the timer expression), in test component operations (in guards or events of alt statements or altsteps, see clause 20.2), or in initializations of altstep local definitions (see clause 16.2.1), the following operations shall not be present in functions called in the cases specified above, in order to avoid side effects that cause changing the state of the component or the actual snapshot and to prevent different results of subsequent evaluations on an unchanged snapshot:

requirements.original: a) All component operations, i.e. create, `start (component),` `stop (component),` `kill,` running (component), alive, done and killed (see notes 1, 3, 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain a component operation (`create`, `start` (component), `stop` (component), `kill`, `running` (component), `alive`, `done` or `killed`).
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- a) All component operations, i.e. create, `start (component),` `stop (component),` `kill,` running (component), alive, done and killed (see notes 1, 3, 4 and 6).

requirements.original: b) All port operations, i.e. start (port), stop (port), halt, clear, checkstate, send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply, raise, catch, check, connect, disconnect, map and unmap (see notes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain a port operation (`start` (port), `stop` (port), `halt`, `clear`, `checkstate`, `send`, `receive`, `trigger`, `call`, `getcall`, `reply`, `getreply`, `raise`, `catch`, `check`, `connect`, `disconnect`, `map` or `unmap`).
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- b) All port operations, i.e. start (port), stop (port), halt, clear, checkstate, send, receive, trigger, call, getcall, reply, getreply, raise, catch, check, connect, disconnect, map and unmap (see notes 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6).

requirements.original: c) The action operation (see notes 2 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `action` operation.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- c) The action operation (see notes 2 and 6).

requirements.original: d) All timer operations, i.e. start (timer), stop (timer), running (timer), read, timeout (see notes 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain a timer operation (`start` (timer), `stop` (timer), `running` (timer), `read` or `timeout`).
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- d) All timer operations, i.e. start (timer), stop (timer), running (timer), read, timeout (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.original: e) Calling non-deterministic external functions, i.e. external functions where the resulting values for actual inout or out parameters or the return value may differ for different invocations with the same actual in and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a non-deterministic external function.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- e) Calling non-deterministic external functions, i.e. external functions where the resulting values for actual inout or out parameters or the return value may differ for different invocations with the same actual in and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.original: f) Calling the rnd predefined function (see notes 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call the `rnd` predefined function.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- f) Calling the rnd predefined function (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.original: g) Changing of component variables, i.e. using component variables on the left-hand side of assignments, and in the instantiation of out and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT use a component variable on the left-hand side of an assignment.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- g) Changing of component variables, i.e. using component variables on the left-hand side of assignments, and in the instantiation of out and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.original: g) Changing of component variables, i.e. using component variables on the left-hand side of assignments, and in the instantiation of out and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT pass a component variable as actual parameter to an `out` or `inout` formal parameter.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- g) Changing of component variables, i.e. using component variables on the left-hand side of assignments, and in the instantiation of out and inout parameters (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.original: h) Calling the setverdict operation (see notes 4 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call the `setverdict` operation.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- h) Calling the setverdict operation (see notes 4 and 6).

requirements.original: i) Activation and deactivation of defaults, i.e. the activate and deactivate statements (see notes 5 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `activate` or `deactivate` statement.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- i) Activation and deactivation of defaults, i.e. the activate and deactivate statements (see notes 5 and 6).

requirements.original: i) Activation and deactivation of defaults, i.e. the activate and deactivate statements (see notes 5 and 6).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `deactivate` statement.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- i) Activation and deactivation of defaults, i.e. the activate and deactivate statements (see notes 5 and 6).

requirements.original: j) Calling functions and deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters (see notes 7 and 8).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or a deterministic external function with `out` or `inout` parameters.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- j) Calling functions and deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters (see notes 7 and 8).

requirements.original: k) Calling functions and external functions with @fuzzy formal parameters and variables (see notes 4 and 9).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or external function that has `@fuzzy` formal parameters or `@fuzzy` variables.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition

readings: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or external function that has `@fuzzy` formal parameters or declares `@fuzzy` variables.

A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT call a function or external function with `@fuzzy` formal parameters, and SHALL NOT reference `@fuzzy` variables.
ambiguity.issue: The scope of 'and variables' is unclear (variables of the called function vs. variables referenced by the calling function); the first reading is used. Item m) covers referencing fuzzy variables anyway.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- k) Calling functions and external functions with @fuzzy formal parameters and variables (see notes 4 and 9).

requirements.original: l) The setencode operation (see note 8 and clause 27.9).
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT contain the `setencode` operation.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- l) The setencode operation (see note 8 and clause 27.9).

requirements.original: m) Referencing lazy or fuzzy variables, parameters or templates that have not been declared deterministic.
requirements.canonical: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT reference a lazy or fuzzy variable, parameter or template that has not been declared deterministic.
requirements.condition: a value returning function is called in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, a guard or event of an alt statement or altstep, or an initialization of an altstep local definition

readings: A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT reference a `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` variable, formal parameter or template unless it is declared with the `@deterministic` modifier.

A function called (directly or indirectly) in a receiving communication operation, a timeout operation, an alt statement or altstep guard or event, or an altstep local definition initialization SHALL NOT reference a `@lazy` or `@fuzzy` object unless the referenced object's evaluation is otherwise known to be deterministic.
ambiguity.issue: 'declared deterministic' is not tied to an explicit syntax in this clause; the first reading (the @deterministic modifier on the lazy/fuzzy declaration) is used. Item m) also overlaps with item k) for fuzzy objects.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- m) Referencing lazy or fuzzy variables, parameters or templates that have not been declared deterministic.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: The use of operations send, call, reply, raise, and action causes an error, i.e. all communication are to be made explicit and not as a side effect of another communication operation or the evaluation of a snapshot.
requirements.canonical: The use of the operations `send`, `call`, `reply`, `raise` and `action` in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because all communication is to be made explicit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 2: The use of operations send, call, reply, raise, and action causes an error, i.e. all communication are to be made explicit and not as a side effect of another communication operation or the evaluation of a snapshot.

requirements.original: NOTE 3: The use of operations map, unmap, connect, disconnect, create will lead to an error, i.e. all configuration operations are to be made explicit, and not as a side effect of a communication operation or the evaluation of a snapshot.
requirements.canonical: The use of the operations `map`, `unmap`, `connect`, `disconnect` and `create` in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because all configuration operations are to be made explicit.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 3: The use of operations map, unmap, connect, disconnect, create will lead to an error, i.e. all configuration operations are to be made explicit, and not as a side effect of a communication operation or the evaluation of a snapshot.

requirements.original: NOTE 4: Calling of non-deterministic external functions, rnd, running, alive, read, checkstate, setverdict, referencing fuzzy objects and writing to component variables causes an error because this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot, thus, e.g. rendering deadlock detection impossible.
requirements.canonical: Calling non-deterministic external functions, `rnd`, `running`, `alive`, `read`, `checkstate` or `setverdict`, referencing fuzzy objects and writing to component variables in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because it may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot (e.g. rendering deadlock detection impossible).
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 4: Calling of non-deterministic external functions, rnd, running, alive, read, checkstate, setverdict, referencing fuzzy objects and writing to component variables causes an error because this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot, thus, e.g. rendering deadlock detection impossible.

requirements.original: NOTE 5: The use of operations activate and deactivate causes an error because they modify the set of defaults that is considered during the evaluation of the current snapshot.
requirements.canonical: The use of the `activate` and `deactivate` operations in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because they modify the set of defaults considered during the evaluation of the current snapshot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 5: The use of operations activate and deactivate causes an error because they modify the set of defaults that is considered during the evaluation of the current snapshot.

requirements.original: NOTE 6: Restrictions except the limitation on the use of out or inout parameterization in restriction j) apply recursively, i.e. it is disallowed to use them directly, or via an arbitrary long chain of function invocations.
requirements.canonical: The restrictions of clause 16.1.4, except restriction j) on out or inout parameterization, apply recursively, i.e. the restricted operations SHALL NOT be used directly or via an arbitrarily long chain of function invocations.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 6: Restrictions except the limitation on the use of out or inout parameterization in restriction j) apply recursively, i.e. it is disallowed to use them directly, or via an arbitrary long chain of function invocations.

requirements.original: NOTE 7: The restriction of calling functions and deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters does not apply recursively, i.e. calling functions that themselves call functions with out or inout parameters is legal.
requirements.canonical: A function called from a snapshot-evaluation context MAY call functions that themselves call functions or deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters, because restriction j) does not apply recursively.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 7: The restriction of calling functions and deterministic external functions with out or inout parameters does not apply recursively, i.e. calling functions that themselves call functions with out or inout parameters is legal.

requirements.original: NOTE 8: Using out or inout parameters and the setencode operation causes an error because this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
requirements.canonical: Using out or inout parameters or the `setencode` operation in a function called from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because it may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 8: Using out or inout parameters and the setencode operation causes an error because this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.

requirements.original: NOTE 9: Calling functions and external functions with @fuzzy parameters causes an error, because fuzzy objects are re-evaluated each time referenced and this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
requirements.canonical: Calling functions and external functions with `@fuzzy` parameters from a snapshot-evaluation context IS an error, because fuzzy objects are re-evaluated each time they are referenced, which may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 16.1.4 -- NOTE 9: Calling functions and external functions with @fuzzy parameters causes an error, because fuzzy objects are re-evaluated each time referenced and this may lead to different results of subsequent evaluations of the same snapshot.
